question: Will the September 2026 US jobs report show year-over-year average hourly earnings growth of 3.1% or higher?

calls.reasoning: Threshold decomposes to a cents-level question: Sep 2025 AHE = $36.70, so a 3.1% print requires Sep 2026 >= $37.82, i.e. a MoM gain of at least +$0.07 from August's $37.75. Recent increments average +$0.080 over 6 months and +$0.096 over 12, and 15 of the last 19 months (79%) cleared +$0.07 — the required move is slightly BELOW trend, which favors YES. The Sep 2025 base month itself rose +$0.08 (exactly trend), so there is no adverse base effect this month. TradingEconomics shows a 3.1% consensus for the Oct 2 release. Against that: the labor market is cooling, the last two 6-month increments include two +$0.06 months, and the threshold sits only ~0.03pp below the trend-continuation value, so one soft month flips it. Treating Sep level as ~N($37.83, $0.04) gives ~0.64; the empirical frequency gives ~0.73-0.79; I settle at 0.66, discounting the raw frequency for decelerating wage growth. No prediction market prices this contract (Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi searched, none found). Shutdown delay risk is timing-only per the fine print.
calls.reference_class: Monthly changes in the seasonally adjusted level of private-sector average hourly earnings (CES0500000003), Jan 2025 - Aug 2026 (19 observations), asking how often the one-month gain was >= $0.07
